West.text: Western India combines strong sunlight with large land availability. Rajasthan and Gujarat are especially important for utility-scale solar, while Maharashtra also has a large estimated technical potential.
West.strategy: Utility-scale solar parks + industrial and rooftop solar

North.text: Northern India includes very high theoretical potential in areas such as Jammu & Kashmir, while practical development varies because of terrain, land use and accessibility.
North.strategy: Mixed utility-scale, rooftop and terrain-aware deployment

Central.text: Central India has strong utility-scale opportunity in Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, with favorable land conditions in several districts and growing renewable-energy infrastructure.
Central.strategy: Large solar parks + agricultural and distributed applications

East.text: Eastern India has meaningful solar opportunity, but dense population, agriculture and climate conditions can reduce the feasibility of very large solar parks in some areas.

South.text: Southern India has strong irradiation in many areas and includes several major solar states. Rooftop, industrial and utility-scale solar can all play major roles.

North-East.text: North-East India has solar opportunity, but cloud cover, terrain, ecosystem sensitivity and transmission access can limit large projects. Distributed systems may be more suitable.
North-East.strategy: Distributed, rooftop and resilient local systems

states.name: Rajasthan
states.insight: Rajasthan has the highest estimated solar potential in the legacy state-wise dataset, supported by high solar irradiation and extensive arid land.

states.name: Jammu & Kashmir
states.insight: Jammu & Kashmir shows very high theoretical potential, though terrain and accessibility affect practical deployment.

states.name: Maharashtra
states.insight: Maharashtra combines strong solar potential with industrial electricity demand and a large grid system.

states.name: Madhya Pradesh
states.insight: Madhya Pradesh has strong utility-scale potential with relatively favorable geography in many districts.

states.name: Andhra Pradesh
states.insight: Andhra Pradesh has major solar potential and already plays an important role in renewable-energy deployment.

states.name: Gujarat
states.insight: Gujarat benefits from strong irradiation, dry conditions and extensive deployment-friendly land parcels.

states.name: Ladakh
states.insight: Ladakh shows high solar-resource potential but deployment depends strongly on infrastructure and environmental conditions.

states.name: Himachal Pradesh
states.insight: Himachal Pradesh has notable theoretical potential, although mountainous terrain influences feasibility.

states.name: Odisha
states.insight: Odisha has moderate-to-high potential and good scope for balanced solar development.

states.name: Karnataka
states.insight: Karnataka is important for both utility-scale and distributed solar strategies.

states.name: Uttar Pradesh
states.insight: Uttar Pradesh has a huge electricity-demand base where rooftop and distributed solar can be especially meaningful.

states.name: Chhattisgarh
states.insight: Chhattisgarh has useful utility-scale potential and room for further solar growth.

states.name: Tamil Nadu
states.insight: Tamil Nadu has strong demand-side opportunity and an active renewable-energy ecosystem.

states.name: Assam
states.insight: Assam has meaningful solar opportunity, particularly for distributed applications.

states.name: Bihar
states.insight: Bihar can benefit significantly from distributed and rooftop solar because of land pressure and dense demand.
